body: For the reference, `6ffffff6f723` is an exception handler frame inside `msvcrt.dll` or `ntdll.dll`, we probably can symbolicate it, but not sure if it is worth doing (since it will require handling both PDB and DWARF at the same time, and looking for PDBs for system libs). But at least listing all loaded dynamic libraries and their load addresses might be useful (I'll check it later in a separate PR).

Could the module name also be included? I find that is often enough information to attribute blame (in engine, in gdextesion, or in some loaded system dll). This is what I was proposing in my PR #116259

> Could the module name also be included?

Not sure if it would work with `libbacktrace`. And not sure if there's any practical use for it, printed trace is primarily for use in bug reports, and we won't know specific versions of system libs, so addresses no in the main module will be useless.

> > Could the module name also be included?
> 
> Not sure if it would work with `libbacktrace`. And not sure if there's any practical use for it, printed trace is primarily for use in bug reports, and we won't know specific versions of system libs, so addresses no in the main module will be useless.

Showing module name with relative offset (RVA) was something I contributed in my other PR because I found it useful as a builder on top of Godot. My team has a GDExtension which can have bugs and it made it easy to see if the crash was due to our GDExtension instead of the Godot executable itself.

@bruvzg  Thank you for including the module names! One thing that I think needs to be fixed that was in my PR is an existing bug in the windows SEH handler that surfaced ~20% of the time due to improper string copying. The bug is pre-existing but is now visible due to use of `SymGetModuleInfo64`. See my comment here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116259/changes#r2805937226

Essentially SymLoadModule64 was being passed copies of strings using std::vector<char> without including the null terminator.
